title: Does an Executable Validator Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated Network Configuration Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced a single shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the identical candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) enforced structured workflow policies and could trigger at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; paired contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We expand methodological detail, representative diagnostics grounded in archived validator traces and task manifests, reproducibility guidance tied to the preregistered artifacts, and discuss construct/external validity limits and design recommendations for future confirmatory studies.

sections.introduction:
Large language models promise to convert operator intent into actionable network configuration commands, potentially improving NetOps productivity. Yet syntactically plausible command sequences can violate temporal and stateful workflow invariants (for example, changing MTU without an enforced shutdown or performing an unsafe uplink switchover) and thus produce semantic failures visible only in closed-loop execution. Prior executable-benchmark and tool work recommends integrating deterministic verification, emulation, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before enactment. Measuring the marginal contribution of such validators requires an experimental lens that exposes stateful, temporal, and group-level invariants rather than token- or syntax-level correctness alone.

We performed a preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) to isolate the marginal effect of an executable emulator validator and a bounded repair policy on identical generator outputs. The mechanistic research question was: does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To attribute any differences exclusively to the validator/repair subsystem, we used a shared-initial-candidate paired design: for each task we recorded a single generator output (gpt-5-mini) and scored that same candidate under both baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (validator±repair) conditions.
sections.related_work:
Executable benchmark and tool research for NetOps underscores that token- or syntax-level metrics fail to capture important closed-loop errors: make-before-break violations, group availability infringements, and ordered-operation invariants that manifest only during enacted state transitions. Recent executable-benchmark efforts and tool descriptions (for example, NetConfArena, Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair, and Aether) provide empirical evidence that closed-loop emulation detects failure classes missed by static checks [https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23179; https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22513; https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18233].

A second literature strand studies tool-augmented LLM agents and bounded-autonomy guardrails (veto layers, canaries, generate→validate→repair). Surveys and architectural reports argue for delegating safety-critical checks to deterministic solvers or emulators and for runtime validation to reduce operational risk (see reviews and system papers in agentic NetOps literature). Our study complements these lines by changing the experimental lens: prior generator-focused studies often conflate generator variance with verification efficacy, whereas our shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair marginal effects for identical generator outputs. This distinction explains why different experimental choices lead to different operational inferences about repair utility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1 prior to execution. The plan specified a paired-binary confirmatory design with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (edge, core, leaf–spine) of 40 tasks each. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified confirmatory test was the exact two-sided McNemar. A paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified. The preregistration defined exclusion rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic reset controls, and sensitivity analyses.

Task generation and structured payload. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural-language intent, an explicit required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, level). Workflow_policies such as must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break patterns were encoded in the payload and enforced by the executable validator as structured, executable checks rather than heuristic text matches.

Shared-generation paired design. For each pair we issued one shared generation call to the declared model (gpt-5-mini) and reused that identical shared candidate for both conditions. This produced model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). The design removes generator variance across pairs and attributes any discordance solely to validator or repair actions. A known trade-off is that when the generator produces valid candidates across the task bank the validator has no opportunity to exercise repair; this trade-off was explicit in the preregistration and is central to interpreting the observed ceiling outcome.

Validator and repair semantics. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), an executable state checker that (a) applies the shared candidate in an emulator seeded from the task's initial_state, (b) enforces workflow_policies encoded in the task payload, and (c) emits a structured validator_trace recording validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation_codes, and repair_applied (boolean). The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair iteration when validator.violation_count > 0; repair prompts and provider traces (if produced) were archived. In this execution validator.violation_count = 0 and repair_applied = false for every guarded episode.

Instrumentation, contamination controls, and deterministic reconciliation. The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets between tasks, container checksum verification, and provider-call audits. Provider-call accounting reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120, and cache_hit_count = 0. Contamination heuristics included duplicate-output detection and cross-condition cache-key reuse detection; none were triggered. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed pair accounting: complete_pair_count = 120; planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Scoring and primary outcome. Each paired episode produced a binary semantic outcome: pass (semantic_success = 1) when the emulator-observed final_state satisfied the task's expected_final_state and required_sequence constraints under the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule implemented by the validator, and fail (semantic_success = 0) otherwise. The validator also emitted structured score_reason_code values (for example, VALID_CONFIGURATION).
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions. Condition-level summaries: baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rate = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table was n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. The paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; therefore no repair-provider-call artifacts exist.

Per-topology and difficulty strata. The deterministic partition produced 40 tasks per topology class and the observed successes were uniform across classes (Edge: 40/40 baseline and guarded; Core: 40/40; Leaf–spine: 40/40). Representative difficulty metadata from archived task manifests shows levels labeled medium, hard, and very_hard and required_command_count values ranging from 2 up to 6 for sampled tasks, confirming the harness included nontrivial workflow constraints even though no semantic violations occurred.

Representative diagnostics. Archived validator traces and per-episode scoring artifacts show, for representative episodes, that normalized_response equaled normalized_reference_answer, parsed_command_count matched required_command_count, validator.validation_after.valid = true, observed_touched_field_count > 0 for tasks that changed multiple interfaces, and validator.repair_applied = false. Example documented patterns include shutdown→configure→restore and make-before-break uplink switchover; in each archived example the shared generator candidate satisfied the required_sequence and workflow_policies so no repair was necessary.

Statistical interpretation. The confirmatory McNemar test reported p = 1.0 because there were zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0). The preregistered bootstrap CI is degenerate at [0.00, 0.00] under our resampling scheme because every resample reproduces the same paired contingency when no discordant pairs exist. Importantly, the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline failure ≈ 0.40 targeting an absolute reduction of 0.15; the observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions and renders the original power justification inapplicable for this execution.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the ceiling outcome. The shared-generation paired design isolates the validator/repair subsystem: if the generator already produces valid candidates for the selected task bank and frozen prompt strategy, the guard cannot improve an already-perfect baseline. The observed degenerate contingency table and CI are consistent with this ceiling: the validator observed zero violations and therefore did not apply repairs across 120 guarded episodes.

Design trade-offs and concrete recommendations. Our findings illustrate a practical trade-off between internal validity (shared-generation controls generator variance) and the ability to exercise repair behavior. Supported, preregistered, artifact-grounded recommendations for future confirmatory work include:
1) Independent generation per condition: allow separate generator draws per condition so the guarded pipeline can intercept generator errors introduced by sampling or prompt instability; analysis must then account for generator variance (for example with stratified or hierarchical models). This change increases external relevance for operational deployments where generator outputs vary.
2) Controlled prompt perturbations: prespecify perturbation variants on a subset of tasks to increase the incidence of generator-induced violations while preserving paired blocks for internal control; perturbation arms should be treated as prespecified exploratory strata in the analysis plan.
3) Task stratification toward high-complexity cases: allocate more pairs to tasks labeled 'very_hard' or with high dependency_rule_count and required_command_count to raise the probability of generator mistakes and thereby exercise repair mechanics.
4) Expanded repair budget in exploratory arms: allow more than one repair iteration to study repair convergence dynamics and repair-call costs (instrument repair_provider_trace accounting when repair_applied=true).

Operational implications and auditability. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (checked rules, touched fields, violation codes, and repair_applied flags) enhances operator auditability and post-hoc diagnosis. Provider-call audits and deterministic reconciliation artifacts support transparent accounting of model calls (model_calls_used = 120), cache statistics (cache_miss_count = 120), and stage counts (shared_initial_generation = 120) which are useful for compliance and governance in production settings. The experiment underscores that claims about repair benefits require experimental framing aligned to generator error rates: under a frozen, well-calibrated prompt and the provided synthetic task corpus, the guard was idle by design.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strong for this run: deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audits, zero technical exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity is limited because workflow_policies and task payloads are synthetic encodings; the validator enforces canonical workflows but does not model full vendor heterogeneity or partial telemetry observability. External validity is constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity is affected by the statistical ceiling: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40; observed baseline = 0.00 invalidates that assumption and makes the McNemar test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size. These validity assessments and the raw artifacts supporting them are archived with the run for independent verification.

Value of artifact-rich preregistration. A second, methodological contribution is procedural: preregistered workflows that combine explicit structured task payloads, executable validators that report fine-grained traces (violation_codes, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count), and deterministic reconciliation permit transparent diagnosis of why a confirmatory test produced a null or ceiling result. The archived artifacts enable precise follow-up experiments that relax shared-generation constraints, vary prompt strategies, or compare multiple generator families under identical executable tests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and demonstrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear when generators sometimes produce invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we show how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. The archived artifacts support follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and evaluate more production-rooted corpora to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
